newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB extends losses on competition probe.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB extends losses on competition probe.

text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Plc extended recent losses in early trading on Friday after news late yesterday that the European Commission would probe the company's exclusive UK soccer deal.
The stock was also weighed down by negative comment on News Corporation's plan confirmed yesterday to mortgage part of its stake in Sky as part of a $1 billion debt issue.
BSkyB shares were down 21-1/2p at 575 by 0710 GMT.
Competition commissioner Karel Van Miert said he would study the exclusive deal BSkyB reached with the English Football Association and would look at the four-year duration of the contract.

Louise Barton, analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite, said she thought BSkyB's soccer deal would survive any competition probe but said it had created uncertainty over the stock, which surged to a record 698p on October 21.
"All it is doing is adding the the grief," Barton said. "before, people were willing to ignore the bad news."
Barton said News Corp's warrant plan was a signal that Rupert Murdoch thought BSkyB shares had become overvalued -- triggering a change in sentiment towards the stock.
"To me it signal the fact that Murdoch thinks it is overvalued and he can get a better return from his interests elsewhere in the world," Barton said.

Separately, comment in the influential Financial Times Lex column added to the downward pressure on BSkyB shares. Lex said the warrant issue "amounts to a bet by Rupert Murdoch that BSkyB shares will rise less than 20 percent over the next five years."
It also said the 11 percent stake owned by Granada Group Plc in Sky had become less saleable as a result of News Corp's move. Granada was down 13-1/2p at 870-1/2.
